task.description: Idiom-review the diff on feature/WF02-REQ025-20260817 (git diff main...HEAD, focus on lib/letflow/event_store.ex and lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex). This is Letflow's first multi-table Ecto.Multi atomic transaction and went through 2 rework iterations on SECURITY-REVIEWER's INV-8 gate (struct-shaped input crashes) before passing -- confirm the final fix pattern (is_map/1 combined with is_struct/1 exclusion) is applied consistently and isn't a one-off patch that leaves the module's overall input-validation style inconsistent. ALSO: the design doc flagged OQ-5 as a MAJOR open question needing your explicit confirmation -- read lib/letflow/design/req025-event-append.md Section 9's OQ-5 in full, and REQ-023's own acceptance criteria/moduledoc language about instance_projections being 'event-store scope for schema, EE-01/S3 scope for meaningful population' -- decide explicitly whether M6's insert-if-absent (creating an instance_projections row with a default ACTIVE status on a brand-new instance's very first append) is within REQ-025's scope or oversteps into EE-01/S3 territory that hasn't landed yet. This is a real scope-boundary judgment call, not a rubber-stamp -- answer it explicitly in your handoff either way.
acceptance_criteria: idiomatic-vs-crutch, supervision, type-safety-gap, and scope-creep questions all explicitly answered
OQ-5 (instance_projections insert-if-absent scope question) explicitly confirmed or rejected, with reasoning, not silently passed through

result.summary:
Reviewed git diff main...HEAD for lib/letflow/event_store.ex (new) and lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex (edited), plus lib/letflow/design/req025-event-append.md in full, docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-023/REQ-025 entries, req023-event-store-schema.md's instance_projections sections, the shipped InstanceProjection schema module, and the instance_projections migration.

JOB 1 -- standard idiom review (all four points explicitly answered):
(1) Idiomatic vs. crutch -- the Ecto.Multi usage is idiomatic, not hand-rolled. build_multi/1 composes one Multi.run/3 per step with clear atom names (:active_instance_guard, :assign_sequence, :idempotency, :insert_event, :store_oversized_payload, :update_projection); the changes accumulator is used correctly (assign_sequence's result is read back in insert_event and update_projection); on_conflict:/conflict_target: is used for both real upserts (M2's instance_sequence insert-if-absent, M3's idempotency claim, M6's projection upsert) instead of a racy check-then-insert; the FOR UPDATE-equivalent lock uses Ecto's lock("FOR UPDATE") query composition, not a raw SQL string (matches INV-7). The pre-transaction phase (P0-P6, entirely outside Repo.transaction/Multi) is an unusual but explicitly reasoned choice (moduledoc + inline comment cite the design doc's invariant-8/9 interpretation), not an accidental deviation from the more common 'validation as Multi step 1' idiom. No crutches found -- e.g. no hand-rolled retry loop standing in for what on_conflict: already gives atomically, no manual existence-check-then-insert race anywhere.
(2) Supervision -- N/A, confirmed explicitly. Both changed modules (Letflow.EventStore, Letflow.TenantProvisioning) are plain context modules with zero process/OTP surface: no use GenServer/Supervisor/gen_statem, no spawn, no process registration, nothing touching Letflow.InstanceSupervisor. Diff introduces no new process and collapses no existing isolation.
(3) Type-safety gaps worth noting (asked for even unprompted): (a) interpret_transaction_result/1 ends in a catch-all clause ({:error, _failed_operation, reason, _changes} -> {:error, reason}); this matches design doc Section 6.3's stated fallback, but nothing at compile time forces this function to be revisited when a 7th Multi step is added later -- a sum-typed match (Rust/OCaml) over the known Multi step-name set would force an exhaustiveness check at the point a new step is introduced, where Elixir will silently route an unrecognized step's error through the generic branch instead. Not a defect today (correctly implements the documented fallback) but worth watching as more Multi steps are added. (b) @type append_error() re-lists Registry's error atoms (:tenant_not_provisioned, :unknown_event_type, {:payload_validation_failed, ...}) as a hand-copied subset of Letflow.EventStore.Registry's own error union rather than referencing/importing a shared type -- if Registry's error union changes shape in a future requirement, nothing here forces this @type (or its exhaustive interpret_transaction_result/1 handling) to be updated; a runtime error or a missed case in a future property test is what would surface the drift, not a compiler.
(4) Scope creep -- no new behaviours/macros/generic plumbing introduced ahead of need in the reviewed diff considered as ordinary Elixir code (the tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 addition is a narrowly-scoped pure function directly required by the settled 0003 addendum, not new abstraction). The one real scope-creep finding is substantive enough to be its own item -- see JOB 2 below (M6's insert-if-absent).

validate_metadata/1's is_struct guard (INV-8 rework item), consistency check: the final guard `when not is_map(metadata) or is_struct(metadata)` appears in exactly one place in the module (grep-confirmed) -- it is not a one-off patch bolted onto an otherwise-different validation style, it is correctly scoped to the one function that actually needs it. Every other attrs-derived value in this module is extracted via Map.get/2 or Map.has_key?/2 (reject_tenant_id, fetch_uuid, fetch_payload, fetch_idempotency_key, fetch_event_type), both of which are struct-safe (structs are maps under the hood, so Map.get/has_key? behave identically for a struct or a plain map) -- so none of those call sites carry the same crash risk validate_metadata had. validate_metadata is the ONLY function in the file that calls Enum.* (Enum.find_value/3) over caller-supplied, unknown-shaped input -- confirmed by grepping the file for Enum.* (the only other hit, Enum.any?/2 in sequence_conflict?/1, iterates Ecto-internal changeset.errors, not caller input, so it carries no equivalent risk). The top-level append/2 entry guard (is_map(attrs) and is_list(opts)) does tolerate a struct-shaped attrs, but does not crash on one -- traced through every fetch_*/reject_tenant_id call and confirmed none of them enumerate attrs generically, they only Map.get specific known keys. Net: the fix is applied exactly where the risk class (Enumerable-requiring code over caller input) actually exists, not inconsistently scattered or missing from a sibling case that needed it. Worth a light 'watch' note only: if a future edit adds any Enum.*/for-comprehension over attrs itself (not just individual extracted fields), it will need the same is_struct exclusion, and nothing here would flag that need automatically.

Checked against docs/anti-patterns.md: no existing entry applies directly to this diff (entries cover toolchain availability, status-file overwrite, and timestamp estimation, none of which this diff touches).

JOB 2 -- OQ-5 scope-boundary decision (real judgment call, not rubber-stamped): CONCLUSION -- M6's insert-if-absent behavior OVERSTEPS into EE-01/S3 territory. This is a FAIL requiring rework, not a pass-through.

Reasoning: REQ-023's own text (docs/requirements.yaml:958-964) says instance_projections' *schema* is event-store scope but its 'meaningful population at instance-start' is EE-01/S3 territory, 'not built yet -- do not read this migration as instance-engine work landing early.' The question is whether creating a bare row (instance_id, tenant_id, status: :active, last_event_seq) on an instance's first append counts as that deferred 'meaningful population,' or is merely incidental bookkeeping the event store needs for its own writes. Four independent pieces of evidence tip this toward 'oversteps,' not 'incidental':
(1) REQ-025's own acceptance-criteria text (docs/requirements.yaml:1077-1078) describes step 7 as 'instance_projections update: last_event_seq and updated_at updated in the same transaction' -- update only, no insert-if-absent language -- in sharp textual contrast to step 2 (line 1060), which explicitly calls out 'insert-if-absent per event_store.md's First append to a new instance SQL pattern' for instance_sequence. The same requirement's own author was explicit about insert-if-absent where it applies (instance_sequence) and silent about it where it doesn't (instance_projections); that asymmetry reads as deliberate, not an omission the implementer should fill in.
(2) req023-event-store-schema.md itself (lines 158, 1071) frames the deferred item as 'Meaningful population of instance_projections AT INSTANCE START,' owned by 'S3/EE-01.' 'At instance start' names a specific lifecycle event -- the engine deciding an instance now exists and is active -- which is exactly what creating a status: :active row on first append does, dressed up as 'just the bare row its own writes need.' Deciding that an event arriving for an instance with no projection row should silently mean 'start it now, as ACTIVE' is an implicit instance-lifecycle policy call, not a storage mechanic.
(3) The shipped Letflow.EventStore.InstanceProjection schema module (lib/letflow/event_store/instance_projection.ex) is the ONLY one of REQ-023's six event-store schema modules that exposes an update_changeset/2 (its own moduledoc says so: 'unlike every other schema in lib/letflow/event_store/, it legitimately exposes an update_changeset/2') -- a strong signal REQ-023 anticipated append() only ever UPDATING this table, never creating it. The REQ-025 design doc's own M6 implementation notes (Section 10) that update_changeset/2 is 'deliberately NOT used' in favor of insert_changeset/2 + on_conflict: -- i.e. the implementation routes around the exact tool REQ-023 appears to have built for an update-only contract.
(4) The design doc's own counter-argument ('without this, no instance could ever receive its first event under current scope') is not decisive: R-Co's actual architecture plausibly requires an instance to be started by the engine (creating the projection row with definition_id/current_nodes/status together) before any event is ever appended to it -- meaning it is CORRECT, not a gap, that append/2 cannot originate a new instance during S2 before EE-01/S3 lands. TEST-DESIGNER can still exercise M1's terminal-instance and update paths by seeding an instance_projections row directly via Repo.insert (test fixture setup does not need to go through production append() code), so 'nothing else can test this' does not hold either.

The design doc's own Section 9 OQ-5 anticipates this outcome explicitly: 'if REVIEWER disagrees, append/2 would need an entirely different contract (e.g. refusing to append to an instance with no pre-existing projection row), which is a materially different, not incrementally different, design.' That is the correct characterization -- this is not a one-line ELIXIR-DEV patch, it requires CODE-DESIGNER to redesign M1's 'no row found' branch and M6's create-vs-update split (e.g. M1 treating 'no row' as {:error, :instance_not_started} or an equivalent named error rather than :new_instance, and M6 becoming update-only) plus a corresponding error-taxonomy addition, before ELIXIR-DEV re-implements and this gate is re-run.

issues.summary: M6's insert-if-absent creation of an instance_projections row with a default ACTIVE-equivalent status on an instance's first append oversteps into EE-01/S3's 'meaningful population at instance-start' territory that REQ-023 explicitly defers; REQ-025's own acceptance-criteria text only ever says 'update' for this table (unlike instance_sequence's explicit insert-if-absent callout), and InstanceProjection is the only event-store schema module REQ-023 gave an update_changeset/2, which M6 bypasses in favor of insert_changeset/2 + on_conflict:.
issues.recommendation: Route back to CODE-DESIGNER to redesign M1's 'no projection row found' branch and M6's create-vs-update split -- e.g. M1 returns a distinct error (such as {:error, :instance_not_started}) instead of :new_instance when no row exists, and M6 becomes update-only, using InstanceProjection.update_changeset/2 as REQ-023 appears to have intended. ELIXIR-DEV re-implements against the revised design; this gate re-runs afterward.

result.next_action: FAIL -- do not route to TEST-DESIGNER. Route back to CODE-DESIGNER to redesign instance_projections' M1/M6 create-vs-update contract per OQ-5 finding, then to ELIXIR-DEV for re-implementation, then re-run Step 2d (REVIEWER).
